ross-parry-211.description: Hand-coloured plate of the cliffs on the northwest Greenland coast whose snow is stained deep red, with the printed position latitude 76 degrees 25 minutes N. John Ross sent a boat ashore on 17 August 1818 under Mr Ross, midshipman, and Mr Beverley, assistant surgeon, to bring back samples, and the botanist Robert Brown, examining them in London, could get no further than entering the colouring matter in his plant list as minute globules of a doubtful genus of the algae. It is now identified as the snow alga Chlamydomonas nivalis, and red snow is still measured on this coast as a feedback that darkens melting ice.

ross-parry-227.description: The large folding meteorological register kept aboard John Ross's ship the Isabella through the voyage of 1818: the daily record of barometer, thermometer, wind and weather, ruled across the whole opened sheet.

ross-parry-119.description: West half of the large folding chart of the coasts newly charted by the expedition, showing Bathurst Island, Graham Moore's Bay and the southern shore worked along the outward passage. It was engraved for William Edward Parry's published journal of the first voyage.

ross-parry-246.description: The volume's summary chart of the whole voyage, plotting the ships' track from Hudson Strait through Foxe Basin to Igloolik and the Strait of the Fury and Hecla against the wider geography from Baffin Bay to Hudson Bay, with the coasts newly charted by this and the preceding expedition shaded to show what had been added to the map. It was engraved for William Edward Parry's journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-049.description: Title page introducing the chronometer appendix, which used eight chronometers to fix longitude throughout the voyage and, cross-checked against lunar distances, established the position of Winter Harbour and of the coast newly charted along Melville Island. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.
